findings.issue: V0 still surfaces Firebase setup as dashboard action work. Evidence: `dashboard.build()` calls `capabilities_status.run_status(profile=None)` and writes the full capabilities cache, while `profile=None` treats every capability as active and `operator_console` converts `needs_setup` capabilities into `needs_action`, including `firebase-dashboard`. Recommendation: scope dashboard V0 capability/action output to local/core requirements or explicitly exclude/demote Firebase dashboard capability items

`serve` will miss normal edits inside existing plan directories. Evidence: `_watched_paths()` watches `plans_root` and per-plan `audit/` dirs, while `_max_mtime()` only checks one directory level; modifying an existing `plan.md`, `features.json`, or `INBOX.md` usually does not bump the plan directory mtime. Recommendation: recursively hash/mtime relevant source files or enumerate known plan/dashboard source globs, and add a test that edits an existing plan file.

The watch loop includes generated output in its watched sources, so rebuilds can trigger more rebuilds. Evidence: `_watched_paths()` includes `out_dir`, and each rebuild writes files into `state_out_dir`; `last_mtime` is set to the pre-build value. Recommendation: do not watch generated `dashboard/state`, or recompute the baseline after rebuild while excluding generated files.

The serve watcher tests only add a new plan dir and force `plans_root` mtime, so they do not catch missed edits or rebuild feedback. Evidence: `test_serve_watch_loop_rebuilds_on_source_change` creates a second plan and calls `utime(plans_root)`. Recommendation: add tests for editing an existing plan source file and for no rebuild when only generated state files change.
